steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spread butter all over the pork tenderloin. Season with salt, pepper, and thyme. Combine garlic powder, apricot preserves, honey, and sherry in a separate bowl.

Roast the pork in the preheated oven for 30 to 40 minutes. Remove the pork from the oven and brush with the apricot sauce. Return the pork to the oven. Continue roasting, basting occasionally with the remaining sauce, until the pork is no longer pink in the center, about 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Apricot Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: Apricot preserves and honey add a fruity sweetness to this simple pork tenderloin.

review.reviewBody: Forget the butter...too messy! I rubbed my two tenderloins with olive oil and the seasonings. Everything else about the recipe is perfect and the pork was SO moist, tender and delicious! The leftovers make the most wonderful pork sandwiches. Thanks....a hit with the family, and so easy too!

I seared the pork in avocado oil first and wrapped it in aluminum foil then placed it on a rack. I baked at 325 degrees on a convection oven. I removed the foil and raised the temperature to 375 degrees after covering with the glaze. I also used fresh thyme and fresh garlic and ginger and I replaced the honey with half maple syrup and half balsamic vinegar. Remove from heat when 5 degrees under temperature and tent with foil. Let rest for about ten minutes.

It was delicious, this will be my go-to pork tenderloin recipe. I made a few personal adjustments: I melted the butter and brushed it on the pork loin then added salt and pepper. I mixed the rest of the melted butter with honey, apricot preserve, minced garlic and thyme to add later. I cooked it longer to reach 165F, about an hour and 15 minutes altogether. I basted it with the butter/preserve every 15 minutes.

Very nice! I brushed the loin with olive oil, then wrapped it in bacon, seared it in a hot skillet until browned, then reduced the cooking time. Since I didn't have peach, I used pineapple mango spreadable fruit in the sauce and served with coconut rice--will definitely do this one again!

If you follow the recipe without using a meat thermometer, you'll end up w/ 2 pieces of leather. At 350, it takes 3 pounds of meat about 20 minutes to cook to 145. Preheat to 350 and go with what your probe says. Don't waste an entire jar of apricot jam on this. You'll only have time to baste one time by the time the meat is ready. It's a good glaze though, so don't skip on it, just make a lot less of it. Go easy on the thyme! It can get a little funky if you use too much. I'll definitely make this again, but w/ many mods. Don't follow recipe as written.

This was so yummy! Made exactly as written. Heated the leftover baste and added a bit of cornstarch to thicken it a little and drizzled over the sliced pork. 
Served with mashed potatoes.. so good. 
Will definitely make this again. 
Next time I may try it with Apple jam instead...hmm

Loved it. Following the suggestion to use EVOO instead of butter, I roasted the meat for a little under 30 minutes before basting, and took it out a little early as well. We like our pork tenderloin on the medium rare side. I had half the amount of apricot preserves on hand, but it worked fine. I also followed the suggestion to use fresh minced garlic instead of powdered. I heated the sauce mix in the microwave to make it spreadable. I served the meat, sliced in 1/2 inch slices, over a salad of mixed greens (sweet frisee, red oak, lollo rossa, green tango), that had been tossed with scallions, mandarin orange sections, and chopped smoked almonds with a homemade dijon vinaigrette. Drizzled the sauce on the meat before serving. It was superb.

I made it without garlic and rubbed the pork with olive oil, then salt , pepper, and thyme. For the glaze I didn't have honey or sherry, so I put apricot jam, molasses,and mead into a saucepan then heated it until the alcohol taste was gone. My husband has dietary restrictions, so no garlic honey, or alcohol. However, it came out delicious and I plan to make it again.

I loved it ...family was okay with it. I browned the loins in a pan first, then added the glaze mix. Cooked it for 30 minutes then started glazing every 5 mins. for a total of 50 mins cooking time. It was still juicy and there was plenty of sauce to put over rice. I have to add that I felt the alcohol needed to cook off and that is why I cooked it in the pan for 10 mins. before glazing the meat with it.

All I had was fresh apricots, so I halved them, lightly touched them with a little olive oil then popped them on the grill for the last 4-5 minutes while my tenderloin that had been coated with fresh thyme, flat leave parsley, kosher salt, pepper and a little orange infused olive oil. The tartness of the grilled apricots went very well with the pork medallions i got out of the tenderloin.

Easy and tasty, will definitely make again. I did add Dijon mustard and some cayenne, which gave a nice counterbalance to the sweet. I used olive oil on the pork instead of butter just for ease and didn’t miss the butter. I would use this sauce as a glaze for ham as well. Really tasty, and the pork was tender to boot.

This was a hit at Christmas Dinner. We had 12 people so I cooked 3 tenderloins. It was more than enough. Plenty of leftovers. I seared them in a large magnalite pot. After searing I put them in the oven in the same magnalite pot for 40 minutes at 350F. Added the glaze and cooked at 250F for 20 minutes. Final internal temp was about 165.

The flavors of this recipe blend together deliciously! The recipe was very easy to follow, and the result was fantastic! Although the recipe did not specify doing this, I flipped the tenderloin when I seasoned it as well as all of the times I basted it. So everything got covered, and it seems that the different flavors were all absorbed by the meat; every bite was full of deliciousness!
I made this, and frankly found it to be quite Betty Crocker Cookbook, sickeningly sweet. May as well make it as a jellyroll using cotton candy.
Love this! I’ve made it several times and had to share the recipe with friends and family!
Love it

I loved the recipe and knew I had some apricot jam in my fridge. Sadly it had gone bad, and I whipped up some organic blueberry jam w/a few frozen cranberries and some lemon juice w/the honey and the sherry. I had the pork tenderloin in the oven so I had to make it fast on the stovetop. It tasted great so I just went with it.. I used fresh garlic instead of powdered, and added a little Siracha sauce before I put it in the oven. Then I basted the meat w/my hastily made tart and sweet “chutney” for the last 10 minutes of cooking. I can’t wait to get some apricot jam and try this as written, but we all know even the best laid plans don’t go our way sometimes. I’m serving it with mashed red skin potatoes and asparagus from our garden. Happy cooking everyone! :)
My family loved this recipe. Wonderful flavors. We’ll definitely make it again. I did not include the honey, it was sweet enough!

I like the idea of the butter. I was going to try the olive oil but decided it would be better with the butter. Apricot sauce really complements the flavor of the pork. Only thing I changed was onion powder for garlic powder. I have a family member who cannot have garlic. It worked just as well and I thought everything still tasted delicious.
The apricot and pork are elegant. I baked a sweet potato and served apricot as it's sauce. Perfect!
